title: Fleet soundcheck + soft-hedge rundown (weekly)
body:
Purpose
Quick standup-style weekly writeup focused on the small, high-leverage changes we ran this week to reduce cold-start pain and buy capacity headroom (soft hedging). This is a working note — playbook edits to follow in Confluence once action items land.

Attendees
Aisha (owner), Marcus, Sofia, Drew, Olga, Paul (SRE), Mandy (capacity planning).

Summary (TL;DR)
- Smoke-run of the "soundcheck" flow completed across us-west1 and eu-west3; median priming reduction for 1k-request burst tests down from 320ms to 210ms on p4d-tier VM pool.
- Soft-hedge experiment: reserved an opportunistic 8-GPU slot pool (preemptible-backed) in apac-south for 48 hours; utilization ~28% but prevented two cross-region fallbacks during simulated overloads.
- Two follow-ups: better priming metric in telemetry (INFRA-4821) and autoscaler tweak to prefer hedged slots for low-latency SLAs (INFRA-4879).

Signals and metrics observed
- Burst test (1k concurrent small text generations, seq_len=128): us-west1 median priming 210ms (prev 320ms), p95 510ms (prev 720ms).
- KV cache hit ratio improved by ~6% after moving priming shard placement rule to hot-path.
- Hedged-slot cost: ~USD 48 over 48h for 8 GPUs (preemptible discount), estimated saved customer-facing fallbacks valued at ~USD 600 in latency SLA impact for two incidents.
- Alert noise: two additional false-positive priming alerts from the new metric edge; worked with observability to tune threshold.

Region notes
- us-west1: primary soundcheck success. Observed a pattern where long-running model instances with >10k tokens accumulated KV eviction thrash — opened a follow-up to cap idle-kv by model (INFRA-4922).
- eu-west3: warmup improvements correlate with smaller batch sizes for short-context jobs. Will adjust default batch-bounds for the zone.
- apac-south: hedged capacity deployed. Need to ensure mem-limit of hedged nodes matches quantized-model footprints (one hedged node OOM'd in a synthetic test).

Incidents & near-misses
- Incident (near-miss): 2026-03-27 04:12 UTC — cross-region fallback triggered during synthetic soak due to unexpected slot reclamation in a partner region. Hedged pool prevented customer-visible errors. Post-mortem draft created.
- Observability gap: priming telemetry did not tag by "route-tier" consistently — causes muddy SLO reports when mixed traffic is sent to the same slot. See INFRA-4821.

Changes rolled this week (high level)
- config: priming shard affinity moved into hot-path (code PR merged: infra-config PR #213).
- autoscaler: temporary heuristic to prefer hedged-pool slots for routes with latency-SLO=true (canary, 24h).
- monitoring: new metric priming_time.v2 and an aggregated priming_count label; alert thresholds adjusted in eu-west3.

Open action items (owner, due)
- INFRA-4821: Tag priming telemetry by route-tier and add per-route priming dashboards (Marcus, 2026-04-02).
- INFRA-4879: Evaluate autoscaler preference fallout for slot churn and roll forward or revert (Sofia + Paul, 2026-04-05).
- INFRA-4922: Implement idle-KV cap per-model to reduce eviction thrash (Drew, 2026-04-09).
- Hedged-node sizing: confirm mem footprint matrix and update hedged pool instance types to avoid OOMs (Olga, 2026-04-01).
- Playbook: draft soft-hedge runbook (Aisha, 2026-04-06).

Risks / concerns
- Cost vs. benefit for small customers: hedged pools make sense for enterprise tenants with tight latency SLOs but increase baseline cost. We need a billing attribution experiment before wide rollout.
- Preemptible dependence: using preemptible-backed hedges works now, but long-term we need a mix that includes dedicated reserve capacity for enterprise commitments.
- Observability maturity: without route-tier tagging, we risk misattributing priming regressions to platform-level issues.

Notes from experiment retros
- Hedging strategy: even a small hedged pool reduced fallback probability significantly during our controlled overloads. Recommendation: keep hedged pool active for 7-day rolling test with A/B of autoscaler preference off/on.
- Priming placement: moving the shard decision to hot-path reduced variance — but increases config churn risk. Add conservative rollout (canary to 2% traffic) and expand.

Meeting decisions
- Approve 7-day hedged-pool extended test (low-cost preemptible nodes) starting 2026-03-30. Responsible: Mandy + capacity team.
- Proceed with INFRA-4821 telemetry tagging as high priority before Monday (Marcus).
- Autoscaler preference to remain canaryed for additional 72h (Sofia).

Useful links / references
- Playbook draft (internal): Confluence link above.
- PR: infra-config PR #213 — priming placement change.
- JIRA: INFRA-4821, INFRA-4879, INFRA-4922.

Appendix (scratch notes)
- Quick checklist for next run: ensure hedged pool has same CUDA/driver version, ensure quantized model docker tags match, prewarm script sets KV-reserve to 128MB for small models.
- Slack snippets: "hedge test: prevented fallback X2" — see #fleet-ops messages on 2026-03-27 05:01.

If anything is missing or you want the raw logs/soak replay traces, ping me and I will attach the S3 link and the replay recipe.

-- Aisha
